Question
========
The CPU time and disk I/Os of 5 programs are given below.

| Program | CPU time (s) | Number of I/O requests |
|---|---|---|
| A | 10 | 27 |
| B | 8 | 17 |
| C | 4 | 11 |
| D | 4 | 3 |
| E | 4 | 2 |

Determine the Pearson correlation between the number of I/O requests and the CPU time, then comment on the meaning of this value.

Solution
========
Means: CPU time 30/5 = 6 s, I/O 60/5 = 12.

Deviations for CPU time: 4, 2, -2, -2, -2. For I/O: 15, 5, -1, -9, -10.

Sum of products = 60 + 10 + 2 + 18 + 20 = 110.
Sum of squared CPU deviations = 32. Sum of squared I/O deviations = 432.

r = 110 / sqrt(32 x 432) = 110 / 117.6 = 0.94.

Comment: a correlation of 0.94 is a strong positive linear relationship, so programs doing more I/O also tend to use more CPU. It says nothing about causality, and with only 5 points it is a fragile estimate.
